title.narrative: #JordanHortiFuture: Towards a More Inclusive and Resilient Horticulture Sector for Smallholder Farmers in Jordan

description.narrative: Mercy Corps in partnership with Wageningen University & Research (WUR), Advance Consulting and Agriterra is implementing the three-year #JordanHortiFuture programme, guided by the overarching goal of enabling smallholder farmers to have an increased income and resilience in a better performing horticulture sector. The Consortium, focusing in Irbid, Ajloun (highlands), and Balqa (Jordan Valley), will adopt an inclusive and layered-approach to address the root causes and challenges of smallholder farmers and value chain actors, both at individual and organization-level, to enhance efficiency, sustainability and profitability of the horticulture sector in Jordan. Ultimately, the programme will contribute to a horticulture sector in Jordan that is inclusive, entrepreneurial, sustainable and resilient for these smallholder farmers. To this end, the programme will target smallholder farmers, but also SMEs and other value chain actors, cooperatives, government agencies, policy makers and financial institutions.

title.narrative: Output 1.2.1: Nature inclusive practices piloted in horticulture sector
Indicator 1.2.1: # of piloted interventions on nature inclusive agriculture

description.narrative: Based on the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), this indicator will capture the number of pilot projects launched by WUR following their research and technical inputs to to test and further finetune the proposed nature inclusive interventions and strategies, and to evaluate and identify approaches to roll-out and bring these interventions and strategies to scale.

comment.narrative: Following land selection, the project team searched for a suitable CBO in the Hashmiyeh area to oversee the pilot's implementation, monitoring, and management. Upon reaching an agreement with "Mehras," sub-grant procedures commenced, including obtaining Government Approval for foreign funding. Unfortunately the MOA did not grant this approval for the CBO to conduct the pilot themselves, as such Mercy Corps will be implementing the pilot directly through an Agricultural Company (Procurement Process). Following completion, NARC will take supervisory responsibility over the pilot area. Moreover, the program has been strategically refined following extensive discussions with stakeholders and working groups, including NARC (National Agricultural Research Centre). As a result, we have agreed to conduct only one targeted pilot project on ancient olive trees. Initially, two additional NIA (Nature-Inclusive Agriculture) pilots were planned with WUR (Wageningen University & Research) and NARC, but these have been reassessed. Both NARC and WUR have decided to shift their focus towards strengthening working groups and enhancing awareness of nature-inclusive practices. This decision allows us to concentrate our efforts more effectively and ensures that potential NIA interventions or practices can emerge organically through the activities of the working groups, aligning closely with our objectives of promoting sustainable agriculture and engaging stakeholders comprehensively.

In progress, The selection of the service provider was guided by criteria such as the company’s location and its experience with similar initiatives. In Y3/Q4, the team finalized a service agreement with Albasata Agricultural Company. A Nature Inclusive Agriculture (NIA) consultant will oversee the technical design and implementation of the pilot, which will continue to be maintained, supervised, and adapted by NARC following the program's conclusion

In progress. A land has been selected and the process of signing a sub-grant agreement with a community-based organization that specifically works in promoting ancient olives in the area. Waiting for gov. approval.

MC and NARC are looking into new options for selecting the area for the pilot in Ajloun as land management and landownership became an issue for contracting and moving forward with the permaculture plan. The next quarter will be more focused in changing the approach of selecting areas.
The process of solicitation for a suitable Agricultural Company began in May. Evaluation of the received offers is expected to proceed in July.

The program worked with the NARC coordinator who developed a comprehensive Nature Inclusive Pilot Design for 4 dunums in Hashameyah that has ancient olive trees. Because Nature Inclusive Agriculture is a holistic approach that focuses on long-term sustainability, the JHF team is looking into implementing this activity through a community based organization in collaboration with the landowners. The premise of such an approach is to ensure that once the programme is concluded, the pilot continues to be maintained, supervised and adapted so as to protect its sustainability.

The selection process was completed for the nature-inclusive agriculture demo site in Ajloun that will introduce the best area that has a heritage Mehras/ancient olive trees. NARC and MC looked into many options in the area of Ajloun, however, many issues have been raised for the land management concern for the farmers.

comment.narrative: AC has finalized the cooperative assessment and has selected 5 cooperatives, 2 in Irbid, 2 in Balqa, and one in Ajloun. The training is schedule to be started 30 Oct. 2022 targeting 20 Cooperative board members.

As part of the efforts to strengthen collaboration and share knowledge between Jordan and the Netherlands, a delegation of Jordanian agricultural cooperatives from the Balqa, Ajloun, and Irbid governorates visited the Netherlands from June 23 to 30. The purpose of the study tour was to assess successful cooperative models and draw from the pioneering Dutch experiences in this domain. During the tour, field visits were organized for various cooperatives in the fields of vegetables, fruits, and financial institutions. These visits provided insights into operational strategies and best practices that foster cooperation and ensure long-term success.

Focus group discussion (FGD) has been conducted on The Impact of the Tax Tariff on Agriculture for Cooperatives with a total number of attendees being 14 (Male 9, Female 5). In addition, during the next quarter a digital marketing training will be organized in Amman for all 15 cooperatives included in the JHF programme. This training will be facilitated by a peer-to-peer expert (agripooler) from the Netherlands and a marketing expert from Jordan. Moreover, a study tour for cooperative leaders and JCC staff will be conducted in June.

In progress, the first 'my coop' training was concluded for 5 corporations. 10 additional cooperatives were selected. Simultaneously, a training needs assessment was conducted. Based on this assessment a training plan has been established for the 10 cooperatives. As a first training activity, 6 cooperatives that are active in growing fruits and vegetables have attended the GAP Lead Farmer training sessions. The full training plan consists of the following activities: Good Agriculture Practices GAP Training (completed), Digital Marketing TrainingMy Coop Training, Financial literacy, Action plan training.
